author: Mark Magnier
description:
Han Zheng, China’s vice-president, called on “major countries” to respect the sovereignty and security of Middle Eastern nations and bring about a two-state solution for the “Palestinian question” on Saturday at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in an implicit dig at the US and Israel.
This came as some analysts questioned why Chinese President Xi Jinping opted not to address the global body given his three-day summit in Washington with US President Donald Trump this week – despite the short...
title: Why Xi Jinping skipped the UN after his Trump summit

author: Vincent Chow
description:
US President Donald Trump is pushing for a rebrand of artificial intelligence (AI) — and looking to get the world’s other AI superpower, China, on board.
All US government documents, and “hopefully the world’s”, will use the term “superintelligence”, or SI, to refer to the fast-evolving technology, Trump said at the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday.
The same day, the US State Department ordered US diplomats to use SI instead of AI in all communications moving forward, the Associated...
title: Amid many thorny issues with China, Trump pushes to rename AI as superintelligence

author: Ling Xin
description:
Chinese researchers appear to have revealed a previously unknown satellite-to-satellite refuelling operation in high Earth orbit, putting the country at the forefront of a technology that could reshape the space race.
In a paper undergoing peer review for the Journal of Deep Space Exploration, the team said China had “successfully provided room-temperature propellant refuelling for a high-orbit BeiDou satellite for the first time”.
The researchers from the state-funded Deep Space Exploration...
title: Claims China’s BeiDou satellite was refuelled in orbit could change space race

author: Regina Ip
description:
As China has emerged as a peer competitor to the United States in many areas, an increasingly familiar question is whether it has become a superpower. The question, however, may rest on a definition of power that belongs to another era.
China possesses many attributes traditionally associated with great powers: a large population, vast territory, a major economy, advanced technological capabilities and growing military strength. Yet Beijing describes China as a “major country” rather than a...
title: How China is seeking to transform the meaning of great power

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
China and the United States have agreed to pursue a new military crisis-communication pact following the summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, according to Beijing, potentially giving commanders another mechanism for managing dangerous encounters across the Indo-Pacific.
China’s Foreign Ministry said on Saturday that the two militaries had agreed to conclude a memorandum of understanding on “crisis communication and prevention” as soon as possible.
The two militaries already have...
title: Beijing says US, China to pursue military crisis-communication pact

author: Vincent Chow
description:
There is little question that Jensen Huang and Lisa Su, the heads of US semiconductor chip giants Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), had secured two of the best seats in the house at the White House state dinner on Thursday evening: at the head table alongside the two presidents and their wives.
But what remains unclear is how much progress they were able to make on their primary goal of restoring access to the Chinese market, amid entrenched opposition to that happening in both China and...
title: Why US chip controls took a back seat at the Xi-Trump summit

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
When Donald Trump arrives in Shenzhen for the November Apec summit, he will face a Chinese leader even more confident than the one who left Washington this week after a state visit heavy on pageantry but light on concrete deliverables.
Experts attributed this confidence to three key factors – a newly upgraded bilateral framework seeking a “constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity”, the warmer tone during Xi’s three-day visit, and – crucially –...
title: 3 top reasons Trump will face a stronger Xi Jinping at November Apec forum in China

author: Igor Patrick
description:
The Brics-founded New Development Bank could help launch a fund by the end of the year to guarantee cheap loans for poor families in Africa and Latin America, Brazil’s social development minister said.
The scheme would be the Shanghai-based lender’s first financial commitment to Brazil’s global anti-hunger alliance, an initiative sidelined by Washington’s presidency of the G20 this year.
Wellington Dias told the South China Morning Post on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in...
title: China-based Brics bank set for lead role in hunger alliance this year, Brazil says

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Over a private tea session in the White House’s Red Room to mark the end of Xi Jinping’s state visit, US President Donald Trump struck a relaxed tone, marvelling across the table at how fast the Chinese leader had made the trip to America.
“It’s a very fast plane … the fastest plane,” Trump said, in footage captured after the White House TV press pool resumed coverage following a court ruling that restored access to outlets previously banned by the US president.
“[It was due to] its route,” Xi...
title: Why Xi’s flight from China to the US was hours faster than Trump’s in May

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The new US-Denmark-Greenland security agreement could narrow China’s room to engage in the Arctic – particularly in resource-rich Greenland – and potentially push Beijing closer to Russia, Chinese experts on the matter said.
According to observers, the deal – signed on Tuesday – could have the broader effect of accelerating the securitisation of the Arctic and making Western Arctic states more cautious about cooperation with China. But it would be unlikely to significantly disrupt China’s...
title: Why US deal on Greenland could narrow China’s Arctic engagement

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Just a month after Saudi Arabia signed a regional mutual defence deal with Pakistan and Turkey, attacks by Yemen’s Houthis against the kingdom’s energy infrastructure and military sites are testing the pact’s limits.
At a hastily convened meeting of the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Friday, military chiefs of the three parties reaffirmed their commitment to collective defence, according to the Saudi Press Agency.
The agency said the talks focused on “intelligence cooperation,...
title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia test limits of Mecca regional security pact

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
First ladies Peng Liyuan and Melania Trump opened a new front in US-China exchanges this week, with their unusually frequent and spontaneous interactions putting a more personal face on ties during the presidential summit in Washington.
The pair charted a parallel path of soft power diplomacy – sharing conversations, cultural outings and moments of apparent warmth during a visit otherwise shadowed by trade tensions, and artificial intelligence and other strategic issues.
According to US-China...
title: How Peng Liyuan and Melania Trump opened a parallel track in US-China diplomacy

author: Gabriel Dominguez,Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s transfer of a former coastguard vessel to the Philippines has triggered a dual controversy – raising concerns over the interests of Taiwanese fishermen and prompting strong criticism from Beijing.
The matter centres on a 61-metre (200-foot) retired cutter handed over to the Philippine Coast Guard through a non-governmental organisation on Monday, as Taipei and Manila expand practical maritime cooperation despite the absence of formal diplomatic ties.
Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office...
title: Why Taiwan’s coastguard vessel transfer to the Philippines has sparked a double outcry

author: Albee Zhang,Josephine Ma
description:
China and the United States have struck a new deal on coal and agreed to open a communication channel on “super intelligence” incidents, according to the White House.
The commitments were outlined in a fact sheet on Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington this week.
It said China had agreed to import at least 10 million tonnes of coal from the United States next year and again in 2028.
The statement also said the two sides would “continue to work on” US concerns about China’s exports...
title: Xi-Trump summit: China and US to open ‘super intelligence’ communications channel

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage of Peng Liyuan during the Xi-Trump summit. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. China’s first lady Peng Liyuan projects glamour and soft power on world stage
China’s first lady Peng Liyuan is again stepping into the international limelight as she travels to Washington with President Xi Jinping this week.
2. Peng Liyuan and Melania Trump renew acquaintance as Xi arrives in US

Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan...
title: China’s first lady Peng Liyuan shines during Xi-Trump summit: everything you missed

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is reportedly trying to arrange a phone call with Donald Trump following the US president’s nostalgic invocation of the alliance with China during World War II, references that sent shock waves through Tokyo.
Trump made the references as he welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday for his first state visit to Washington in over a decade.
Both Trump and Xi repeatedly invoked their nations’ wartime alliance against Japan in their...
title: Will the Trump-Xi wartime ally nostalgia prompt a Japanese rethink on China ties?

author: Chao Kong
description:
Offshore wind farms can reduce the coverage of shore-based radar systems and create areas where targets become harder to detect, according to a new study.
The researchers found that at a range of 5km (3 miles), effective radar coverage fell by 6.9 per cent while blind spots increased by 14.9 per cent.
The research, published online last month in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Radio Engineering, was conducted by Professor Liu Zunnian and his team from Qingdao Technological University and the...
title: Offshore wind farm could create radar blind spots and ‘ghost’ targets, Chinese study warns

author: Mark Magnier
description:
During their three-day summit that ended on Friday, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping worked overtime to underscore their increasingly close relationship even as the meeting produced few concrete deliverables.
But the fact that the two economic and military giants are talking – and pledging to talk some more – suggests some period of relative stability ahead, certainly relative to last year’s all-out trade war, chest-thumping and market turmoil, said analysts, companies...
title: Xi-Trump atmospherics welcomed but mask structural rifts: analysts
